# Feature: Code Generation & Agent Repair Loop

## 1. Feature Goal

**ID**: FEAT-106
**Source Plan**: `.spec-lite/plan_mvp.md`

Turn an approved description of a file plus a sentence of plain English into **a specific, immutable, digest-identified version of Python that the agent believes works, and can show its working for** — without that belief being worth anything on its own.

Concretely:

- The agent writes Python, writes pytest tests for it, runs them, reads the failures, and repairs. It does this through four application-owned tools; it has no filesystem access, no shell, and no network. FEAT-102's `noTools: 'all'` still stands, and everything the agent writes lands in the database first and on disk second.
- The tests run against a **synthetic fixture the application builds from the approved disclosure payload** — the same column names, the same types, the same ten sample rows, plus ~200 rows of application-synthesized data drawn from the recorded statistics. **The real file is never opened during generation.** The plan row's own sentence — *"agent progress messages alone do not authorize execution"* — is not a policy this row states, it is a property this row makes structurally true: there is no code path in FEAT-106 that reads an upload's bytes.
- Every repair attempt is counted **in the database, at the tool boundary**. The fourth `run_tests` call is refused by the application with a tool result telling the agent to finalize its best version. A system-prompt instruction is not a limit.
- Every candidate is sealed into a `code_version` with a SHA-256 over its whole file set. That digest is what FEAT-107 binds its verification results to and what FEAT-108 executes. "What was checked, and which exact code it applies to" (plan §6) is answered by a join, not by a convention.
- What comes back out of pytest is **not trusted**. In a milestone with no isolation boundary (D03), generated Python can read any file the server process can, and its stdout flows straight into the model's context on the next repair turn. So test output goes through FEAT-105's default-deny `filterDiagnostics` before the agent ever sees it, and is recorded as a `diagnostics` transmission against the person's consent. Decline the diagnostics scope and the repair loop does not run — the first failure stops and asks, exactly as FEAT-105 promised.

For the person running the preview, the visible change is: after approving the disclosure, the transcript fills in — *"Attempt 1 of 3 — wrote `main.py` (84 lines) and `test_main.py` (3 tests). 1 failing: `ValueError` in `main.py` line 41."* … *"Attempt 2 of 3 — 3 passing."* — with the code readable at every attempt, and a plain line under it saying **"Tested against 200 synthetic rows built from your column descriptions. Your real file has not been read."** If all three attempts fail, the run stops and offers a text box: *"Tell me what I got wrong and I'll try again."*

### Decisions applied (resolved 2026-09-22)

The plan lists FEAT-106 as blocked by **D07** (repair limits, review UX) and **D14** (three versus five attempts, time and spend limits). Both were resolved with the user before this spec was written, along with two design forks this row could not avoid. Recorded here because `plan_mvp.md` §5 still lists D07 and D14 as open; each resolution is scoped to *this row* and does not close the decision globally.

| Decision | Resolution | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| D14 — attempt limit | **`AUTOMATE_MAX_GENERATION_ATTEMPTS`, default `3`**, documented as provisional against the rest of D14. An attempt is one `run_tests` invocation; the cap is enforced by `COUNT(*)` over `generation_attempt`, not by the system prompt. | Memory's Security section says explicitly *"do not hardcode a value until it is decided"*, so a constant was not an option. Three is the preview default because the fourth attempt on a model that has not converged in three is usually the same idea again at full price; five is one env var away for anyone who disagrees. **This does not resolve D14** — time, spend, concurrency, and file limits stay open, and this row's other limits are provisional in the same way FEAT-103's concurrency and FEAT-104's file limits are. |
| D14 — time and spend | **Wall clock `AUTOMATE_GENERATION_TIMEOUT_MS` default `600000` (10 min), enforced across the whole `generating` phase. Spend `AUTOMATE_MAX_GENERATION_COST_USD` default `0` = disabled**, accumulated from `turn_finished` usage and enforced between turns when enabled. | The cost cap ships **off** deliberately. FEAT-102 never materializes a `costUsd` the provider did not report, so a cap that is on by default would silently never fire for providers that report nothing — a limit that does not limit is worse than an absent one, because people plan around it. On when a number is set, visibly off otherwise. |
| D07 — repair visibility | **Visible and non-blocking.** Every attempt streams into the transcript with its code, its test counts, and its filtered failure output. The loop never parks to ask permission to try again. | A run that stops after each failed attempt spends a person's attention on a decision they have no information to make — they cannot read the Python, which is the entire premise of the product. Information without an interruption is the honest trade. |
| D07 — on exhaustion | **Settle `failed`, then offer "try again with guidance"** — a free-text hint that seeds a **new** execution (`trigger = 'rerun'`, `retry_of_execution_id` set, `guidance` stored), reusing the existing consent and the persisted clarification answers. | The failed run stays failed and stays readable; the retry is a new row rather than a mutation, so history keeps both. Approval of code *before it runs against real data* is not here — that is FEAT-107's gate, and putting a second approval in front of it would train people to click through the one that matters. |
| Test data (design fork) | **Synthetic fixtures only.** The fixture is built from the approved disclosure payload and application-synthesized values, seeded deterministically from `upload.sha256`. FEAT-106 contains **no code path that opens an upload's stored bytes.** | The alternative — running agent-written code against the real file during the loop — executes unverified code against the person's data before any verification gate exists, which contradicts the plan row's own sentence. The accepted cost is real: a script that passes on 200 synthetic rows can still fail on row 40,000 of the real file. That failure is FEAT-107/108's to catch, and the honest place to say so is the UI, which TASK-014 requires to say it. |
| Python runtime ownership (ordering fork) | **FEAT-106 defines the `PythonRunner` seam and ships a minimal `uv`-backed implementation** sufficient to run pytest in an attempt directory. **FEAT-108 replaces the implementation** with locked dependency policy, resource limits, and the real-data execution leg. | FEAT-108 owns the Python runtime but comes later in plan order, so FEAT-106 is otherwise un-implementable as written. This is the same seam-then-fill pattern FEAT-103 used for `RunStrategy` and FEAT-105 filled. The seam lives in `packages/core` with no Node built-ins so FEAT-108 changes one file, not a call graph. Queued in TODO.md. |

### Assumptions carried (flag if wrong)

- **`CodeGenerationRunStrategy` wraps FEAT-105's `DisclosureRunStrategy`; it does not replace it.** FEAT-105 shipped the strategy that assembles approved context, registers `request_clarification`, and records transmission receipts, and said plainly that "FEAT-106 subclasses or wraps it." This row wraps: the disclosure half is untouched, and this row adds the code-generation system prompt and four more tools to the same `buildRun` result. Every disclosure guarantee FEAT-105 tested continues to hold unchanged, and TASK-016 re-asserts them rather than assuming they survived.
- **D05 is not resolved here.** The test loop needs *some* packages to import. This row ships a **provisional four-package set** — `pandas`, `openpyxl`, `plotly`, `pytest` — in one named constant, `GENERATION_DEPENDENCY_SET`, marked provisional against open D05 and owned by FEAT-108 thereafter. It is the smallest set that lets a CSV/XLSX preparation-and-reporting script and its tests import successfully. Queued in TODO.md.
- **`execution.retry_of_execution_id` is the column `data_model.md` calls `parent_execution_id`.** FEAT-103 deliberately did not adopt it, deferring the feedback re-run to FEAT-107. The guidance retry needs the same link, so it is created here under a name that describes what it is. **FEAT-107 must reuse this column** rather than adding a second one, and may extend `execution.trigger`'s CHECK with `'feedback'` if it needs to distinguish the two. Queued in TODO.md.
- **Tool arguments are elided from the transcript, not from the record.** `write_script`'s argument *is* the script — persisting it in `conversation_event.payload` as well as in `code_file` would store every version twice and replay all of it to the browser on every reconnect, while creating two copies of the code with nothing guaranteeing they match. `AgentToolDefinition` gains one optional field, `redactArgsInEvents`, and FEAT-103's `TaskSession` applies it **before persist and therefore before broadcast**. The full arguments still reach `execute()`. There is exactly one authoritative copy of generated code: `code_file`.
- **`finalize_script` is not a gate.** It accepts a version whose tests never passed, and records that fact. Refusing would make FEAT-106 the thing that authorizes execution, which is precisely what the plan row forbids and what FEAT-107 exists to do. The application tracks; it does not adjudicate.
- **The `manifest.json` contract is stated and observed here, enforced in FEAT-107.** The system prompt requires generated code to declare its outputs in `AUTOMATE_OUTPUT_DIR/manifest.json` (memory's artifact model), and `run_tests` *records* whether a valid manifest appeared during the test run. Turning that observation into a pass/fail condition is FEAT-107's, and FEAT-109 owns registering the artifacts.
- **No artifact registration, no real-data run, no verification checks.** A test run's `output/` directory is scratch and is discarded with the attempt. Nothing in this row writes to `artifacts/` or creates an `artifact` row.
- **No retention policy for code versions or attempts.** They cascade with the execution and otherwise persist; a 3-attempt run holds roughly 40 KiB of code. D12 owns retention and is open. Queued in TODO.md.

## 2. Data Model (Granular)

`.spec-lite/data_model.md` exists but, per `plan_mvp.md` §2, predates the confirmed decisions and is **not the authoritative schema** (reconciliation tracked in `.spec-lite/TODO.md`). It is nonetheless the closest prior art for this row, and its treatment is worth stating explicitly:

- **Rejected: `execution.script_content` / `script_language` / `verification_log` / `phase_timings` as columns on `execution`.** A single `script_content` column can hold one version of one file. This feature produces up to three versions of two-or-more files each, and the whole point is that verification binds to a *specific* one. Flattening that into a column would make "which code did we check?" unanswerable the moment a repair happens — the exact failure plan §6 warns about.
- **Rejected: `script_language`'s `'shell'` value.** D05 confirms Python only; shell output is deferred. A CHECK admitting `'shell'` would be structure for deferred scope.
- **Adopted: the idea that the executed script is an immutable snapshot**, kept in the database rather than read off disk at run time. Promoted from a column to `code_version` + `code_file`.
- **Adopted: `parent_execution_id`'s purpose**, under the name `retry_of_execution_id` (see §1).

Conventions carried from FEAT-101/102/103/104/105: `snake_case` singular tables and columns; timestamps `INTEGER` epoch seconds with Drizzle `{ mode: 'timestamp' }`; booleans `INTEGER` with `{ mode: 'boolean' }`; JSON as `TEXT`; `INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT` for entities whose ids appear in file paths; schema defined in driver-independent `drizzle-orm/sqlite-core`.

### Entities & Attributes

- **code_version** — one candidate, sealed and immutable. The unit FEAT-107 verifies and FEAT-108 executes.
  - `id` (INTEGER) — `PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT`. Appears in the REST path and in FEAT-107's future verification rows.
  - `execution_id` (INTEGER) — `NOT NULL`, `FK → execution.id ON DELETE CASCADE`.
  - `attempt` (INTEGER) — `NOT NULL`. 1-based. The draft being assembled carries the attempt number it will be sealed as, so the transcript can name it before it is sealed.
  - `status` (TEXT) — `NOT NULL DEFAULT 'draft'`, `CHECK(status IN ('draft','sealed','tested_pass','tested_fail','superseded'))`. `draft` is mutable and holds no digest; every other value is immutable. A draft becomes `superseded` when the agent writes a new file set without ever running tests.
  - `content_digest` (TEXT) — `NULL` while `draft`, `NOT NULL` once sealed. Lowercase hex SHA-256 over `canonicalStringify` (FEAT-105) of the file set as `[{path, sha256}]` sorted by path. **This is the identity a verification result binds to.** A digest that changes means different code, full stop.
  - `dir_path` (TEXT) — `NOT NULL`. Relative to the data root: `scripts/{executionId}/attempt-{n}`. Relative so `AUTOMATE_HOME` can move without rewriting rows (FEAT-104's rule).
  - `entrypoint` (TEXT) — `NOT NULL DEFAULT 'main.py'`. The file FEAT-108 will run.
  - `is_final` (INTEGER boolean) — `NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`. Set by `finalize_script`.
  - `tests_passed` (INTEGER boolean) — `NULL` until tested. Recorded, not enforced — `is_final` with `tests_passed = 0` is a legal and meaningful state, and FEAT-107 is the one that cares.
  - `declared_inputs` (TEXT) — `NULL` until finalized. JSON `[{fileRole, sheet?, requiredColumns: [{name, type}]}]` — the input contract the agent says the script needs. FEAT-111's compatibility check reads this; FEAT-107 may check it against the profile.
  - `declared_outputs` (TEXT) — `NULL` until finalized. JSON `[{filename, type, title, description}]` matching memory's manifest shape.
  - `summary` (TEXT) — `NULL` until finalized. The agent's own plain-English description of what the script does. **Model output, therefore untrusted input to the DOM.**
  - `sealed_at` (INTEGER) — `NULL` while `draft`.
  - `created_at` (INTEGER) — `NOT NULL DEFAULT (unixepoch())`.

- **code_file** — one file of one version. The authoritative copy; the file on disk is a projection of this row, written by the application, never by the agent.
  - `id` (INTEGER) — `PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT`.
  - `code_version_id` (INTEGER) — `NOT NULL`, `FK → code_version.id ON DELETE CASCADE`.
  - `path` (TEXT) — `NOT NULL`. Relative, forward-slash normalized, no leading slash, no `..`, no drive letter — validated at the tool boundary and again here, because a path from a model is user input by another route.
  - `role` (TEXT) — `NOT NULL`, `CHECK(role IN ('script','test','support'))`.
  - `content` (TEXT) — `NOT NULL`. The file, verbatim. Capped at `AUTOMATE_MAX_SCRIPT_BYTES`.
  - `byte_size` (INTEGER) — `NOT NULL`. UTF-8 length. `CHECK(byte_size >= 0)`.
  - `sha256` (TEXT) — `NOT NULL`. Per-file digest; the version digest is built from these.
  - `created_at` (INTEGER) — `NOT NULL DEFAULT (unixepoch())`.

- **generation_attempt** — one `run_tests` invocation and its outcome. **This table is the limit.** The cap is `COUNT(*)` over it, so a model that ignores its instructions still cannot take a fourth turn.
  - `id` (INTEGER) — `PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT`.
  - `execution_id` (INTEGER) — `NOT NULL`, `FK → execution.id ON DELETE CASCADE`.
  - `code_version_id` (INTEGER) — `NULL` only for a refusal that never sealed a version. `FK → code_version.id ON DELETE CASCADE`.
  - `attempt` (INTEGER) — `NOT NULL`. 1-based, matching the version's.
  - `call_id` (TEXT) — the FEAT-102 tool `callId`, so the attempt joins to its `tool_started`/`tool_finished` pair in the transcript.
  - `status` (TEXT) — `NOT NULL DEFAULT 'running'`, `CHECK(status IN ('running','passed','failed','errored','timed_out','aborted','refused'))`. `errored` is pytest failing to start (an import error, a missing runtime); `failed` is tests that ran and did not pass. They read the same to a person and differently to a repair loop, so they are stored apart.
  - `refusal_reason` (TEXT) — `NULL` unless `refused`. `CHECK(refusal_reason IS NULL OR refusal_reason IN ('attempt_limit','time_limit','cost_limit','diagnostics_not_granted','runtime_unavailable'))`. A refusal is **recorded and rendered**, never silent — the same rule FEAT-105 set for a declined clarification, for the same reason.
  - `tests_total`, `tests_passed`, `tests_failed` (INTEGER) — `NULL` when pytest never reported.
  - `exit_code` (INTEGER) — `NULL` when no process ran.
  - `manifest_present` (INTEGER boolean) — `NULL` until a run completes. Whether a parseable `manifest.json` appeared in the run's output directory. Observation, not a gate (§1).
  - `diagnostic_digest` (TEXT) — `NULL` when nothing was returned. SHA-256 of the **filtered** text handed back to the agent.
  - `dropped_line_count` (INTEGER) — `NULL` until filtered. How many raw output lines the allowlist dropped. Surfaced to the person verbatim, because "14 lines were withheld" is the honest rendering of a default-deny filter and a hidden count is a quiet claim that nothing was lost.
  - `duration_ms` (INTEGER) — `NULL` until settled.
  - `started_at` (INTEGER) — `NOT NULL DEFAULT (unixepoch())`.
  - `settled_at` (INTEGER) — `NULL` until settled.
  - `created_at` (INTEGER) — `NOT NULL DEFAULT (unixepoch())`.

  The filtered diagnostic **text** is not stored here — it is stored once, in FEAT-105's `disclosure_transmission.payload_snapshot`, which is the row that records it was sent. `diagnostic_digest` is the join. Two copies of the same bytes in two tables would be two answers to "what did we send?".

- **synthetic_fixture** — the stand-in data one attempt loop tested against. Recorded so the person can see what was tested and so a retry reproduces it.
  - `id` (INTEGER) — `PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT`.
  - `execution_id` (INTEGER) — `NOT NULL`, `FK → execution.id ON DELETE CASCADE`.
  - `upload_id` (INTEGER) — `NOT NULL`, `FK → upload.id ON DELETE CASCADE`. Which real file it stands in for.
  - `file_path` (TEXT) — `NOT NULL`. Relative: `scripts/{executionId}/fixtures/<stored_filename>`. **The filename matches the real upload's `stored_filename`**, so a script that hardcodes it keeps working against the real input later.
  - `format` (TEXT) — `NOT NULL`, `CHECK(format IN ('csv','xlsx'))`. Always the real file's format; a script written against a CSV must not meet a workbook at execution time.
  - `sheet_count` (INTEGER) — `NOT NULL DEFAULT 1`.
  - `row_count` (INTEGER) — `NOT NULL`. Rows per sheet, excluding the header.
  - `sample_row_count` (INTEGER) — `NOT NULL`. How many of those rows are the approved sample rows, verbatim.
  - `byte_size` (INTEGER) — `NOT NULL`.
  - `sha256` (TEXT) — `NOT NULL`. Reproducibility check: the same profile and seed must produce the same bytes.
  - `seed` (TEXT) — `NOT NULL`. Derived from `upload.sha256`, so generation is deterministic and a retry tests against identical data.
  - `created_at` (INTEGER) — `NOT NULL DEFAULT (unixepoch())`.

### Modified entities

- **execution** (FEAT-103) — two nullable columns, no CHECK change:
  - `retry_of_execution_id` (INTEGER) — `NULL`, `FK → execution.id ON DELETE SET NULL`. The run this one was started from after a guidance retry. `SET NULL` rather than `CASCADE`: deleting a failed run must not delete the successful one that replaced it.
  - `guidance` (TEXT) — `NULL`. The person's free-text hint that seeded this execution. **User input, rendered as text, and — like their prompt — it reaches the provider, so it travels through `assemblePromptContext`'s `user_prompt` source, not as application text.**
  - No new `status` value. FEAT-106 lives entirely inside `generating`, which FEAT-103 already reaches. `waiting` is entered only by FEAT-105's clarification tool, which this row keeps registered and unchanged.
- **conversation_event** (FEAT-103, CHECK extended by FEAT-105) — `kind`'s CHECK gains `'code_version_sealed'`, `'test_run_finished'`, and `'generation_settled'`. **Application-owned kinds**, exactly like `user_prompt` and `disclosure_sent`; FEAT-102's `AgentEvent` union is untouched and its type-level test asserting exactly five members continues to pass. SQLite cannot alter a CHECK in place, so migration `0004` performs the standard table rebuild — the second one on this table. TASK-003 asserts existing rows, their `seq`, and the unique index all survive, because a migration that quietly empties a transcript is discovered by a user, not by a test.
- **`AgentToolDefinition`** (`packages/core`, created by FEAT-105 TASK-008) — one optional field: `redactArgsInEvents?: readonly string[]`. Names argument keys that FEAT-103's `TaskSession` replaces with `{ elided: true, byteSize: n }` in the persisted and broadcast `tool_started` event. Does not affect what `execute()` receives. See §1.

### Relationships

- `execution` 1:N `code_version` via `code_version.execution_id` (`ON DELETE CASCADE`). At most `AUTOMATE_MAX_GENERATION_ATTEMPTS` sealed, plus at most one `draft`.
- `code_version` 1:N `code_file` via `code_file.code_version_id` (`ON DELETE CASCADE`).
- `execution` 1:N `generation_attempt` via `generation_attempt.execution_id` (`ON DELETE CASCADE`).
- `code_version` 1:1 `generation_attempt` via `generation_attempt.code_version_id` — one test run per sealed version, enforced by a unique index. A second run of the same bytes would produce a second attempt against an identical digest, which is a repair loop going in circles and must surface as an error rather than burn the budget.
- `execution` 1:N `synthetic_fixture` via `synthetic_fixture.execution_id` (`ON DELETE CASCADE`). One per attached upload.
- `upload` 1:N `synthetic_fixture` via `synthetic_fixture.upload_id` (`ON DELETE CASCADE`).
- `execution` 0:1 `execution` via `retry_of_execution_id` (`ON DELETE SET NULL`). Self-referencing, at most one level deep per retry, arbitrarily deep as a chain.
- `generation_attempt` → `disclosure_transmission` (FEAT-105) by `diagnostic_digest` matching `payload_digest`. Deliberately **not** a foreign key: the transmission row exists only when diagnostics were actually sent, and an attempt that passed sends nothing.

### Indexes & Constraints

- `UNIQUE INDEX code_version_attempt ON code_version(execution_id, attempt)` — attempt numbers are allocated by the application; a duplicate means the allocator lost track of its own state and must fail loudly.
- `UNIQUE INDEX code_version_final ON code_version(execution_id) WHERE is_final = 1` — partial and unique: **one final version per execution**, so "which code was handed to FEAT-107?" has exactly one answer at the schema level.
- `UNIQUE INDEX code_version_draft ON code_version(execution_id) WHERE status = 'draft'` — at most one draft in flight.
- `INDEX code_version_digest ON code_version(content_digest)` — FEAT-107 looks up by digest to bind its results; FEAT-111 looks up by digest to find a previously verified version of the same code.
- `UNIQUE INDEX code_file_path ON code_file(code_version_id, path)`.
- `UNIQUE INDEX generation_attempt_number ON generation_attempt(execution_id, attempt)`.
- `UNIQUE INDEX generation_attempt_version ON generation_attempt(code_version_id) WHERE code_version_id IS NOT NULL`.
- `UNIQUE INDEX generation_attempt_call ON generation_attempt(call_id) WHERE call_id IS NOT NULL` — one attempt per tool call; a duplicate means the tool fired twice for one `callId`, which is a bug.
- `UNIQUE INDEX synthetic_fixture_upload ON synthetic_fixture(execution_id, upload_id)` — one fixture per upload per run.
- `INDEX execution_retry_of ON execution(retry_of_execution_id) WHERE retry_of_execution_id IS NOT NULL`.
- `CHECK(byte_size >= 0)` on `code_file` and `synthetic_fixture`; `CHECK(attempt >= 1)` on both `code_version` and `generation_attempt`.
- `CHECK((status = 'draft' AND content_digest IS NULL AND sealed_at IS NULL) OR (status != 'draft' AND content_digest IS NOT NULL AND sealed_at IS NOT NULL))` on `code_version` — sealed-ness is one fact, not two fields that can disagree.
- `PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON` comes from FEAT-101's client, so `execution → code_version → code_file` and `execution → generation_attempt` cascade for real. TASK-003 asserts it by row count at every level.
- **Invariant enforced in code, asserted in tests**: at most `AUTOMATE_MAX_GENERATION_ATTEMPTS` non-`refused` `generation_attempt` rows exist per execution. Counted at the tool boundary from the database, never from an in-memory tally that a restart would reset.
- **Invariant enforced in code, asserted in tests**: a sealed `code_version`'s `content_digest` equals the recomputed digest of its `code_file` rows, and no `code_file` row may be inserted, updated, or deleted for a version whose status is not `draft`. Immutability is a repository behavior, not a comment.
- **Invariant enforced in code, asserted in tests**: no `synthetic_fixture` file's bytes contain any cell absent from the approved disclosure payload for that upload. Proven with a sentinel in row 11 of a fixture file (TASK-002), the same technique FEAT-105 used on prompts.

### Storage layout

FEAT-106 fills two directories FEAT-101 already creates (`scripts/`, `env/`) and adds no new top-level entries:

```
~/.automate/                            (or $AUTOMATE_HOME)
├── env/                                — the shared uv project (FEAT-101 created the dir)
│   ├── pyproject.toml                  — GENERATION_DEPENDENCY_SET, written by the app   (new)
│   ├── uv.lock                         — committed to the data root, not the repo        (new)
│   └── .venv/                          — uv-managed, never hand-edited
└── scripts/{executionId}/                                                                (new)
    ├── fixtures/                       — synthetic stand-in data; never the real file
    │   └── <stored_filename>           — same name as the real upload, by design
    └── attempt-{n}/
        ├── main.py                     — projection of code_file rows, written by the app
        ├── test_main.py
        └── output/                     — scratch for a test run; discarded, never registered
```

The database is authoritative for code; the disk is a projection written immediately before a test run. Deleting `scripts/` loses nothing but time. A test run's `output/` is scratch — FEAT-109 owns real artifacts and reads from `artifacts/`, which this row never touches.

## 3. Files

**`packages/core`** (platform-agnostic — `packages/web` imports it, so no Node built-ins and no Pi SDK)

- `src/generation/limits.ts` — the named constants fixed by D07/D14: attempt cap, generation wall clock, per-test-run timeout, cost cap, script byte cap, fixture row count, guidance length cap. Each comments the decision that fixed it and marks it provisional.
- `src/generation/code-version.ts` — `CodeVersionView`, `CodeFileView`, `CodeVersionStatus`, and `computeVersionDigest(files)` built on FEAT-105's `canonicalStringify`, so server and client compute the same digest from the same inputs.
- `src/generation/code-path.ts` — `validateCodePath(path, role)`: normalization, traversal rejection, extension and `test_*.py` naming rules. Pure, and shared by the tool and the repository so the two cannot disagree.
- `src/generation/synthetic-fixture.ts` — `buildSyntheticFixture(profile, options): SyntheticTable`, the pure generator. Deterministic, seeded, no clock, no I/O.
- `src/generation/code-contract.ts` — `renderCodeContract(context): string`, the application-authored instructions describing the I/O contract, the manifest shape, the dependency set, and the platform. The **only** place that text exists.
- `src/generation/attempt.ts` — `GenerationAttemptView`, `AttemptStatus`, `RefusalReason`, and `summarizeAttempts(attempts)` producing the plain-English exhaustion summary shared by the API, the transcript, and the UI.
- `src/generation/index.ts` — barrel.
- `src/execution/python-runner.ts` — the seam FEAT-108 fills: `PythonRunner`, `PythonRunRequest`, `PythonRunResult`, `PythonRuntimeInfo`. Types only, no implementation, no Node built-ins.
- `src/contracts/generation-api.ts` — TypeBox: `CodeVersionSummarySchema`, `CodeVersionDetailSchema`, `CodeFileSchema`, `GenerationAttemptSchema`, `SyntheticFixtureSchema`, `RetryRequestSchema`, `WriteScriptArgsSchema`, `WriteTestArgsSchema`, `RunTestsArgsSchema`, `FinalizeScriptArgsSchema`.
- `src/conversation/conversation-event.ts` — **modified**: add `code_version_sealed`, `test_run_finished`, `generation_settled` and their schemas. The `AgentEvent` wrap is unchanged.

## 4. Dependencies

- **FEAT-101** — required in full: `AutoMateError`/`ERROR_CODES`, the Pino logger and its redaction, the error envelope and correlation-id middleware, the Drizzle/`node:sqlite` client and migration pipeline, the repository pattern, `AppPaths` (`scriptsDir`, `envDir`) and its `resolveWithin` traversal guard, the preflight `uv`/Python probes and their per-OS install hints, TanStack Router/Query, the typed API client, and the `ds.*` design tokens.
- **FEAT-102** — required for the provider seam: `AgentSessionOptions.customTools` and `AgentToolDefinition` (extended here by one optional field), `noTools: 'all'` with a name allowlist, the `tool_started`/`tool_finished`/`turn_finished` events, `turn_finished`'s per-turn usage (which is what makes a mid-run cost cap possible at all), `abort()`, and `FakeAgentProvider`, which is how every test here scripts a repair loop with no network.
- **FEAT-103** — required for `task`, `execution`, `conversation_event`, the state machine (`generating` is this row's whole home), `TaskSession` and `TaskSessionRegistry`, the `RunStrategy` seam, `POST /api/tasks`, `POST /api/executions/:id/abort`, the WebSocket transport carrying the new event kinds unchanged, the origin guard applied to the new state-changing route, and the conversation view.
- **FEAT-104** — required for `upload`, `upload_profile`, `upload_column`, `getDisclosureSource`, and the `exceljs` streaming writer already in the dependency set. The fixture builder reads profiles; it never reads `upload.file_path`.
- **FEAT-105** — required, and load-bearing: `DisclosureRunStrategy` (wrapped, not replaced), `assemblePromptContext` as the only prompt construction site, `filterDiagnostics` for every byte of pytest output, `recordDiagnosticTransmission` as the only supported way to get failure output into a prompt, `verifyForTransmission` and the `scope_diagnostics` consent that gates the whole repair loop, `canonicalStringify` for the version digest, `AgentToolDefinition`, and the `request_clarification` tool, which stays registered alongside the four added here.
- **External runtime prerequisites** (verified, never installed — FEAT-101's rule): `uv` and Python 3.11+. FEAT-101's doctor already reports both as **warnings**, so a developer without them reaches a running app and then meets a typed, plain-English `PYTHON_RUNTIME_UNAVAILABLE` at the first `run_tests` — naming the missing tool and the per-OS install command, not a spawn error.
- **External npm dependencies**: **none new.** `exceljs` (FEAT-104) writes XLSX fixtures, `node:crypto` digests, `node:child_process` spawns, and pytest output parsing is string work. A dependency here would sit inside both the privacy boundary and the code-execution path, which is the worst place to add one.

### Not dependencies (deliberately)

- **A Python AST parser, linter, or security scanner in Node.** `ruff` and `bandit` are memory's static-analysis choices and belong to **FEAT-107**, which independently checks the final version. Running them here would make FEAT-106 the verifier and leave FEAT-107 with nothing to do that it could trust.
- **A sandbox, container, or seccomp layer.** D03 says this milestone is explicitly unisolated. A partial measure here would invite exactly the claim the plan forbids.
- **A diff library.** Attempts are shown as whole files. A diff between attempt 2 and attempt 3 is a nice-to-have for a reader who can read Python — not the audience — and it is queued in TODO.md rather than built.
- **FEAT-107/108/109** — this row is provable end to end with no verification, no real-data execution, and no artifact registration: a task is created, a fixture is synthesized, a scripted agent writes code and tests, pytest runs against the fixture, a failure is filtered and fed back, a second attempt passes, and a final version is sealed with a digest. Everything past that point is another row's.

### TASK-002: Synthetic fixture builder — the row that makes "the real file is not read" structural

- [ ] **Implementation**: Add `src/generation/synthetic-fixture.ts` exporting `buildSyntheticFixture(profile: TableProfile, options: { rowCount, seed }): SyntheticTable` where `SyntheticTable` is `{ header: string[]; rows: string[][]; sampleRowCount: number }`. Build it in exactly this order and from exactly these inputs, and **no others**: the header from `upload_column.name` in `position` order; then the profile's approved `sample_rows` verbatim; then `rowCount - sampleRows.length` synthesized rows where each cell is drawn per column from `inferred_type` and `stats` — integers and decimals uniform within `[min, max]` rounded to the observed scale, dates and datetimes uniform within `[min, max]` rendered in the column's `detectedFormat`, booleans from the observed literals, strings as pronounceable filler of length within `[minLength, maxLength]`, and `empty` columns left empty. Where `top_values` exists (low-cardinality columns only), sample from it with its observed frequencies, so a `region` column holds the person's four real regions rather than four made-up words — those values are already in the approved payload. Where `is_high_cardinality` is true, synthesize freely and **never** reuse a sample value outside the verbatim sample rows. Honor `null_count / value_count` as a null rate. Use a small seeded PRNG (xorshift over a 32-bit seed hashed from `options.seed`) declared in-module — **no `Math.random`, no clock, no I/O**, so the same profile and seed always produce identical bytes. Write the header comment stating the invariant plainly: **every literal in the output is either a cell of the approved disclosure payload or a value this function invented; no byte of the source file reaches it by any other route, and adding a parameter that takes the upload's path would defeat the feature.**
- [ ] **Unit Tests**: Two calls with the same profile and seed produce deeply equal output; different seeds differ; the first `sampleRowCount` rows equal the profile's `sample_rows` exactly. A profile with a numeric column bounded `[0, 100]` produces no value outside it across 200 rows; a date column stays inside its range and renders in its detected format; a `null_count/value_count` of 0.25 produces a null rate within ±0.1 over 200 rows; an `empty` column is empty in every row; a boolean column uses only the observed literals. A low-cardinality column's synthesized values are a subset of its `top_values`; a **high-cardinality column's synthesized values appear nowhere in the profile**, asserted by set intersection. **The central test**: a profile whose sample rows are rows 1–10 is paired with a "real file" fixture whose row 11 holds a sentinel string; the built table is serialized and searched for the sentinel, which must be absent — and the same assertion runs over a generated matrix of 50 profiles. A column count of 512 and a row count of 200 complete under a second. A profile with zero columns, a profile with zero sample rows, and a profile with one row each produce a valid table rather than throwing.
- [ ] **Documentation Update**: Invoke **Document** update mode for synthetic fixture generation.
- **Verify**: `pnpm --filter @automate/core test synthetic-fixture` passes; `grep -rn "file_path\|filePath\|readFile" packages/core/src/generation/synthetic-fixture.ts` returns nothing, proving the builder has no route to the real file.

### TASK-006: Code workspace — draft, seal, project to disk

- [ ] **Implementation**: Add `src/generation/code-workspace.ts` with `CodeWorkspace`: `currentDraft(executionId)` returning or opening the draft at the next attempt number; `putFile(executionId, {path, role, content})` validating through `validateCodePath`, enforcing `MAX_SCRIPT_BYTES` with `CodeTooLargeError` naming both numbers, and writing the `code_file` row (replacing an existing row at the same path in the same draft, which is how a model corrects itself mid-attempt); `seal(executionId)` sealing the draft through the repository and then **projecting the files to disk** at `scripts/{executionId}/attempt-{n}/` via `resolveWithin`, creating a clean `output/` subdirectory, and returning the sealed version; `finalize(executionId, versionId, details)`; and `describe(versionId)` for the API. Projection happens **after** sealing and **from the database rows**, never from anything the agent handed in directly — the digest is computed over what was stored, and what runs is written from what was digested, so "what was verified is what runs" is true by construction rather than by discipline. Clean the attempt directory before projecting so a retry cannot inherit a stale file. Never create a directory from a model-supplied string without `resolveWithin`.
- [ ] **Unit Tests** (against a temp `AUTOMATE_HOME`): `putFile` twice at the same path in one draft leaves one row with the second content; at two paths leaves two; a 300 KiB file raises `CodeTooLargeError` rendering both the limit and the actual size and writes nothing; `../../evil.py`, `/abs.py`, and `main.txt` each raise `InvalidCodePathError` and write nothing. `seal` writes every file to disk with content byte-identical to its row, creates an empty `output/`, and returns a version whose digest equals `computeVersionDigest` over the rows; sealing an execution with no files raises rather than sealing an empty version; `putFile` after `seal` raises `CodeVersionImmutableError`. A second attempt seals into `attempt-2/` leaving `attempt-1/` untouched on disk. Re-sealing after a crash mid-projection (simulated by deleting the directory) re-projects from the rows and produces identical bytes — the property that makes the database authoritative. `finalize` sets `is_final`, `entrypoint`, and the declared contracts, and a second `finalize` for the same execution violates the partial unique index.

### TASK-008: `run_tests` tool — the attempt cap, the filter, and the receipts

- [ ] **Implementation**: Add `src/generation/pytest-report.ts` parsing pytest's `-q` summary (`N passed`, `N failed, M passed`, `ERROR`, `no tests ran`) into `{ total, passed, failed, collectionError }`, returning `null` counts rather than throwing on anything it does not recognize — a parser that throws on unfamiliar output would convert a repairable failure into a crashed run. Add `src/generation/tools/run-tests-tool.ts` with empty parameters. `execute(_, ctx)` runs this sequence, in this order, and stops at the first refusal, recording it: (1) `GenerationBudget.claimAttempt(executionId)` — refuse `attempt_limit`, `time_limit`, or `cost_limit`; (2) FEAT-105's `verifyForTransmission(taskId, 'diagnostics')` — refuse `diagnostics_not_granted`, because without it a failure cannot be fed back and the loop is dishonest; (3) `PythonRunner.probe()` + `ensureEnvironment(signal)` — refuse `runtime_unavailable`; (4) `CodeWorkspace.seal(executionId)`; (5) `PythonRunner.run` with `cwd` = the attempt directory, `AUTOMATE_INPUT_DIR` = the execution's fixtures directory, `AUTOMATE_OUTPUT_DIR` = the attempt's `output/`, and `TEST_RUN_TIMEOUT_MS`; (6) parse the report and check `output/manifest.json` for presence and parseability, recording `manifest_present` **without acting on it**; (7) on anything but a pass, hand the concatenated raw stdout+stderr to FEAT-105's `recordDiagnosticTransmission(executionId, raw)` — which filters through the default-deny allowlist, records the `disclosure_transmission`, and returns the filtered text — and return that text to the agent; (8) `markTested`, settle the `generation_attempt`, append `test_run_finished`. The returned tool result is `{ outcome, testsTotal, testsPassed, testsFailed, diagnostics, droppedLineCount, attemptsRemaining, manifestPresent }`. A refusal returns a result naming the reason and instructing the agent to call `finalize_script` with its best version — it is **not** a thrown error, because a refusal is an expected outcome the loop must be able to end on. Write the header comment: **pytest's output is untrusted bytes from unisolated code; it reaches the model only through `recordDiagnosticTransmission`, and a branch that returns raw output defeats FEAT-105 entirely.**
- [ ] **Unit Tests** (against `FakeAgentProvider` and `FakePythonRunner`, no network, no process): a passing run settles `passed`, marks the version `tested_pass`, records `tests_total`/`tests_passed`, and returns **no diagnostics and no transmission row**; a failing run settles `failed`, records a `disclosure_transmission` of kind `diagnostics`, and returns the **filtered** text; **the raw sentinel literal planted in the fake's stderr appears in neither the tool result, the attempt row, nor any conversation event** — the central test of this task, asserted by substring search over the serialized whole. A fourth call at cap 3 is refused with `attempt_limit`, persists a `refused` row, does not seal a version, does not call the runner, and tells the agent to finalize; the cap is read from config, asserted at cap 1 and cap 3. A run with only the context scope granted is refused with `diagnostics_not_granted` before the runner is touched. A missing `uv` is refused with `runtime_unavailable` carrying the install hint. A timeout settles `timed_out` and still records a filtered diagnostic. `pytest-report` parses the four recognized summary shapes and returns `null` counts for `"INTERNALERROR"` and for empty output without throwing. `manifest_present` is `true` for a valid manifest, `false` for absent, and `false` for malformed JSON, and **none of the three changes the outcome**. A second `execute` for the same `callId` hits the unique index and surfaces as an error rather than opening a second attempt.

- **Verify**: `pnpm --filter @automate/server test run-tests` passes with no network and no spawned process; a static guard asserts `run-tests-tool.ts` contains no path from `PythonRunResult.stdout`/`stderr` to a return value that does not pass through `recordDiagnosticTransmission`, and the guard fails when a deliberate raw-return branch is added.

- [ ] **Implementation**: Add `src/generation/generation-budget.ts` with `GenerationBudget`, one instance per execution, owning the **single** place a refusal reason is decided: `claimAttempt(executionId)` reads `countUsed` **from the database** (never an in-memory tally, which a restart would reset to zero and hand the model three more turns), checks the elapsed wall clock against `AUTOMATE_GENERATION_TIMEOUT_MS`, checks accumulated cost against `AUTOMATE_MAX_GENERATION_COST_USD` when that is greater than zero, and returns a grant or a typed refusal. `recordUsage(turn)` accumulates `inputTokens`/`outputTokens`/`costUsd` from FEAT-102's `turn_finished` events, adding only fields the provider actually reported. Extend cancellation so `POST /api/executions/:id/abort` and `drain(timeoutMs)` cancel, in order: a pending clarification (FEAT-105), an in-flight `uv sync`, an in-flight pytest process tree, and then the provider session — **the generated-test and dependency-preparation legs plan §6 requires**, attached to the existing endpoint with no second cancel path. Aborting during a pytest run kills the process tree (asserted through the injected `SpawnFn`), settles the attempt `aborted`, and settles the execution `aborted`; aborting during `uv sync` cancels it; aborting during a pending clarification cancels that first, then the rest, asserted by call order; `drain` performs the same sequence without waiting on a person. ## 6. Cross-Cutting Concerns

- **Data disclosure (D04) — this row is the first consumer of FEAT-105's chokepoint, and it must not widen it.** Three distinct channels could leak here and each is closed by construction rather than by care. The **prompt** goes through the single `assemblePromptContext` call that FEAT-105 built, with the contract entering as `application_text` and guidance as `user_prompt`; TASK-010 re-asserts FEAT-105's byte-for-byte prompt equality rather than assuming the wrap preserved it. The **test data** is synthetic: `buildSyntheticFixture` takes a profile, not a path, and TASK-002's sentinel test proves no unapproved byte survives. The **test output** — the channel FEAT-105 could not test because nothing ran yet — passes `filterDiagnostics` before it reaches the model and is recorded as a `diagnostics` transmission against the person's explicit scope. That third one is load-bearing in a way worth stating: in an unisolated preview, generated Python can read anything the server process can, and its stdout would otherwise land in the model's context on the next repair turn. A default-deny allowlist is the only filter that holds against output nobody anticipated.
- **The repair loop is gated on the diagnostics scope.** FEAT-105 promised that declining it means "a failed run stops and asks instead of auto-repairing". TASK-008 implements exactly that: the first failure is refused with `diagnostics_not_granted` and the loop ends. A person who declined has a run that fails honestly rather than one that silently repairs on data they did not approve sending.
- **Verification binding (plan §6) — this row supplies the identity, FEAT-107 uses it.** A `code_version`'s `content_digest` is computed from the stored rows, and the files on disk are projected from those same rows after sealing. "Which exact code do these results apply to" is a foreign key, and "did the code change after it was checked" is a digest comparison. Nothing is left to the ordering of writes.
- **Auth**: N/A — single-user local deployment, no accounts (memory, D03). The protection added is FEAT-103's `Origin`/`Host` guard extended to `POST /api/executions/:id/retry`, the one state-changing route this row introduces. Without it a page in the developer's own browser could start a run — and therefore spend — on their behalf. Not a full answer to D10; the per-install loopback token remains open and tracked in TODO.md.
- **Error Handling**: New errors extend `AutoMateError` — `GENERATION_ATTEMPTS_EXHAUSTED`, `GENERATION_TIMEOUT`, `GENERATION_COST_LIMIT`, `CODE_VERSION_NOT_FOUND`, `CODE_VERSION_IMMUTABLE`, `CODE_VERSION_NOT_FINAL`, `INVALID_CODE_PATH`, `CODE_TOO_LARGE`, `PYTHON_RUNTIME_UNAVAILABLE`, `FIXTURE_GENERATION_FAILED`, `EXECUTION_NOT_RETRYABLE`. FEAT-101's middleware is the only place that formats an error body. Two audiences need different things and both get it: a **tool error** returned to the model names exactly what to change ("`main.txt` is not a Python file; use a `.py` path"), while a **user-facing** message names the limit, the actual value, and the next step ("This run used all 3 attempts without getting the tests to pass. Tell me what went wrong and I'll try again."). A **refusal is not an error** — `attempt_limit`, `cost_limit`, and `diagnostics_not_granted` are recorded outcomes the loop is designed to end on, rendered plainly, and they never produce a stack trace or a 500.
- **Logging**: Pino. `info` — attempt claimed/settled (execution id, attempt, outcome, counts, duration), version sealed (id, digest, file count, total bytes), version finalized (id, digest, tests passed), fixture materialized (execution id, upload id, row count, byte size), environment prepared (duration, package count), retry created (source and new execution ids). `warn` — an attempt refused with its reason, a wall-clock or cost limit hit, a pytest run that timed out, a missing `uv` at first use. `error` — unexpected failures with the correlation id the client received. `debug` — attempt counts and budget state, spawn arguments **with paths reduced to basenames**. **Never logged**: generated code, raw or filtered pytest output, fixture contents, sample values, the disclosure payload, the person's guidance text, or original filenames. The generated code is the most tempting thing in this feature to log and the one with the clearest reason not to: it embeds column names, and an unbounded log file would hold everything the 64 KiB disclosure bound exists to limit. The database row is the record; the log carries ids, counts, and sizes.
- **Security — untrusted rendered content**: Four untrusted sources converge on this UI, and all four render as text. Generated Python is model output. The agent's `summary` and its declared input/output contracts are model output. Filtered diagnostics originate in code the model wrote. Fixture preview cells are the person's own approved data (FEAT-104's formula-prefix rule applies — a leading `=`, `+`, `-`, or `@` stays literal). TASK-014 tests script, `onerror`, `javascript:`, and formula payloads in each path.
- **Security — the agent has no filesystem, shell, or network tools.** FEAT-102's `noTools: 'all'` stands with an allowlist of exactly five names, none of which reads a path the application did not choose. Every file the agent produces arrives as a tool argument, is path-validated twice (tool boundary and repository), is stored in the database, and is written to disk by the application. This is a real constraint on the *agent*; it is **not** a constraint on the *generated code*, which runs unisolated under pytest and can reach anything the server process can. Those two statements must never be collapsed into one in code, UI, or documentation.
- **Cancellation (plan §6)**: This row adds two of the four required legs to the **existing** `POST /api/executions/:id/abort` — generated tests (process-tree kill) and dependency preparation (`uv sync` cancellation) — joining FEAT-102's generation leg and FEAT-105's clarification cancel. Real script execution remains FEAT-108's leg and attaches to the same endpoint. `drain` performs the same sequence on shutdown. There is no second cancel path and there must not be one.
- **State recovery (plan §6)**: Browser disconnect — the run continues; reconnect replays from `lastSeq` and the code, attempts, and fixtures are re-fetched over REST, so the page rebuilds itself. Server restart — no run resumes; FEAT-103's reconciliation marks the execution interrupted, FEAT-105 settles its pending clarification, and this row's contribution is that **sealed versions, attempt rows, and fixtures all survive**, so the interrupted run is readable rather than a blank. The attempt budget is read from the database, so a restart does **not** hand the model a fresh three attempts. Files under `scripts/` are a projection and are rebuilt from rows if missing.
- **Provenance (plan §6)**: Every run records which code versions were produced, their digests, which tests ran against which fixture (by SHA-256 and seed), which attempt failed and why, what filtered output was sent and when, which version was finalized and whether its own tests passed, and — for a retry — which run it came from and what the person said. FEAT-107 binds verification to the digest, FEAT-110's history detail reads these rows, and FEAT-111's re-run compares `declared_inputs` against a new file's profile.
- **Security posture (D03)**: This milestone is explicitly unisolated, and this is the row where that stops being theoretical: generated Python actually executes here, under pytest, in a uv virtualenv, with the server process's privileges. Nothing in this feature's code, UI, or documentation may describe the virtualenv, the attempt directory, `--no-sync --locked`, or the fixture substitution as a security boundary. What is true and may be said: the agent's *test data* is synthetic, so a bug in generated code cannot corrupt the person's file during generation. What is false and must not be said: that generated code cannot reach other files on the host. Restricted execution remains required before a target-user pilot, and the runner technology is still unselected.
- **Deferred scope guard**: No `ruff`, no `bandit`, no AI code review, no pre-run intent approval, no post-run acceptance, no binding of verification results (FEAT-107). No execution against the real file, no locked dependency policy, no resource limits beyond the two timeouts here (FEAT-108) — `MinimalUvPythonRunner` is explicitly a placeholder behind a seam. No artifact registration, rendering, or download (FEAT-109) — a test run's `output/` is scratch. No history views (FEAT-110). No templates, revisions, or input mapping (FEAT-111) beyond the `declared_inputs` contract this row records for it. No scheduling, URL ingestion, gamification, or tool registry (D08). No shell-script generation or per-task package installation (D05). No retention or purge policy (D12 open).
- **Memory alignment**: One **documented deviation** and two **resolutions of open items**, no silent departures. The **deviation**: memory's Security section says the attempt limit is "pending D14 — do not hardcode a value until it is decided"; this row ships `AUTOMATE_MAX_GENERATION_ATTEMPTS` with a provisional default of `3`, which honors the instruction's substance (no hardcoded constant) while the user's D14 resolution supplies the default. Memory's Data Model note is updated accordingly. **Resolved for this row only**: D05's dependency set exists as a provisional four-package constant, and D14's time/spend limits as provisional env vars — both in the same shape FEAT-103 and FEAT-104 used for their open limits, and both queued in TODO.md. Everything else follows memory as written: the repository pattern with no Drizzle outside `src/db/`, TypeBox on every input, Pino with its redaction rules, the typed error hierarchy, exact pinning (nothing new to pin), `path.join`/`resolveWithin` for every path, `ds.*` tokens, the manifest artifact model, the two-phase generation/execution separation, and the "never log cell contents" rule FEAT-104 set.

## 7. Changeset

> Captured by hooks (`capture-baseline` / `capture-changeset`), not hand-maintained. See `.spec-lite/features/FEAT-106-code_generation_repair/changeset.json` — the authoritative deterministic review scope. `.spec-lite/hooks.json` currently registers no hooks, so that file will be absent until hooks are configured; until then, fall back to the **Files** list in §3 as the review scope.

### Implementation notes and deviations (recorded 2026-09-25 by implement)

- **DEVIATION — migration identity.** drizzle-kit v1 names migrations by timestamp: the migration is `drizzle/20260925044250_damp_otto_octavius/`, and it is the **fifth** migration (FEAT-105 took the fourth), not `0004`. It adds `execution`'s columns with `ALTER TABLE ADD` (no rebuild of `execution`, which would cascade-delete child rows inside the migrator's transaction) and rebuilds only `conversation_event`.
- **DEVIATION — one `generation_settled`, appended at run end.** `finalize_script` does not append it; the generation lifecycle appends exactly one when the run settles. The outcome union gained `incomplete` (the agent stopped without finalizing, the provider failed, diagnostics were not granted, or uv/Python was unavailable). **Exhaustion wins over finalization**: a run whose attempts all failed settles `failed`/`GENERATION_ATTEMPTS_EXHAUSTED` even when the agent obeyed the refusal and finalized its best version — that version stays recorded (`is_final = 1`, `tests_passed = 0`). A run with a final version otherwise settles `completed`, whether or not its own tests passed.
- **DEVIATION — `TaskSession` stays generic.** Instead of constructing the budget inside `TaskSession`, a strategy may return an optional `RunLifecycle` (usage hook, wall-clock deadline, cancel-before-abort, settle). `CodeGenerationRunStrategy` builds the per-execution `GenerationBudget` and `GenerationLifecycle`; `TaskSession` drives it. `RunStrategy.buildRun` may now return a promise.
- **DEVIATION — fixtures are built from the disclosed tables.** `buildSyntheticFixture` accepts a `TableProfile` or a `DisclosedTable`; the service passes the approved payload's tables, so a column or value the degradation ladder left out never reaches a fixture. It reuses FEAT-104's seeded `sfc32` PRNG rather than a new in-module xorshift. CSV fixtures are byte-identical per seed; XLSX fixtures are content-identical (their zip container records write timestamps).
- **Additions.** pytest runs as `python -m pytest -q --tb=native -rfE -p no:cacheprovider` (native frames are the shape FEAT-105's allowlist keeps). Child processes withhold `AUTOMATE_*` (except the two I/O variables), `VIRTUAL_ENV`, and credential-shaped variables — hygiene, not isolation. `validateCodePath` also restricts names to `[A-Za-z0-9_-]`, rejects Windows device names, and reserves `output/`. The write and run tools refuse once a final version exists. `GET /api/executions/:id/attempts` also returns `limits`; `POST …/retry` returns `201 { task, execution }`. `finalize_script`'s column hint names only disclosed columns. `computeVersionDigest` uses a browser-safe SHA-256 in `packages/core` (parity with `node:crypto` asserted). `DisclosureRunStrategy.buildRun` gained optional `extras` so the contract and guidance join the same `assemblePromptContext` call. `FakeAgentProvider` gained tool-calling steps and `enqueue()`. The registry gained `onInterrupted`, which settles attempts a crash left `running` as `aborted`. A retry's guidance is recorded as a second `user_prompt` event.
- **Pre-existing defects found (logged in TODO.md, not fixed here).** FEAT-105: a task with required pre-flight decisions cannot be created (nested transaction) — the retry route seeds answers after its own transaction to avoid it. FEAT-104: a workbook with a native date column fails to profile (`type_confidence = 2`).
- **Not performed.** TASK-014's manual browser check with a scripted provider (no fake-provider wiring exists for the running server). TASK-004's manual `uv` check was performed on Windows: the environment prepared and `import pandas, openpyxl, plotly, pytest` succeeded; with `uv` hidden, `probe()` threw `PYTHON_RUNTIME_UNAVAILABLE` with the install hint.
- **Test location.** Profile fixtures live in `src/__tests__/generation/synthetic-profiles.ts` per memory's test-location rule, not `src/generation/__fixtures__/`.
